bonuses.requirements: Robinhood's Social Trading Feature Opens to Qualified U.S. Users, Coming to Legend DesktopHomeFeedNewsRobinhood's Social Trading Feature Opens to Qualified U.S. Users, Coming to Legend DesktopRobinhood's Social Trading Feature Opens to Qualified U.S. Users, Coming to Legend Desktop10/13 20:15On October 14, Robinhood announced that its social trading network is now open to all qualified users in the United States. CEO Vlad Tenev stated on October 13 that this feature is integrated into the app's information feed, built around users' trades and performance. Users can follow other traders, view shared account activities, and initiate eligible trades directly from posts using the Quick trade feature. Tenev mentioned that Robinhood Social is now available to everyone, allowing users to share charts, profits and losses, and portfolio allocations, as well as receive news and company updates. This feature was initially tested on March 18, targeting the first 1,000 customers who attended the HOOD Summit, followed by an additional 10,000 users in the subsequent weeks. The early version offered verified trading posts, daily and yearly profit and loss statistics, and manual order placement from the information feed; news feeds are planned for future development. Sharing is selective: trades will not be automatically published, and customers can choose which eligible trades to share, as well as disable trading statistics in their profiles. Access and publishable content are restricted. Social is only available in the U.S., and Robinhood excludes licensed securities professionals, individuals associated with regulated financial institutions, and the company's own employees. Its help page indicates that futures and multi-leg options trades currently do not meet publishing criteria. Tenev stated that Social will be available on Robinhood's desktop trading platform, Legend, in the coming weeks.BullishBearishLikeShareDisclaimer：The content above does not represent HTX's positions.，HT

Announcement Just MadeRipple has announced a strategic partnership with Privy, a digital wallet infrastructure provider owned by payments giant Stripe. The collaboration aims to expand use cases for the XRP Ledger (XRPL) by integrating Privy's embedded wallet technology into the network. This integration will allow developers to build applications that facilitate payments using XRP, Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin, and other digital assets on the XRPL without requiring end-users to directly manage private keys or recovery phrases.
